LOO-593 · Autonomous demo evidence · November 4, 2026

Desktop writes run in the server.

Review the measured improvement and the actual app behavior. No new product decision is needed to finish validation. This page does not approve merging.

Built from scratch/direct-write-demo.md, scratch/server-performance/results.md and the retained native screenshots. The Markdown notes hold the durable record.

About 8× faster for the measured rename

Warm median / p95, msCLI child per writeDirect server
Session rename87.38 / 105.3010.77 / 20.63
Roadmap read26.94 / 34.4228.00 / 52.67
First subscription frame31.64 / 46.6333.40 / 47.55
Checkpoint21.84 / 31.3221.66 / 28.49

Thirty warm samples after discarding the first, using the same Swift harness on debug helpers and private Machines. Background host work was not controlled. This is request latency for a small fixture, not full UI latency.

Reads did not become faster. The single restart-and-read observation rose from 278 to 458 ms; server RSS rose from 244.5 to 255.5 MiB. Both idle CPU samples rounded to 0% over five seconds. No startup or memory improvement is claimed.

Before: an empty local repository

Open Loopflow Direct Writes.app in /Users/jack/.lf/demos/loo593-direct-ioi_wowv. This is an isolated live app using the real configured provider, not the installed app or a mocked UI.

Create a Task

Click New Task, enter a title and click Start. Expected: a Task, separate worktree and its conversation appear. Observed: Task 0a58e8 was created entirely in Desktop. Its research Graph stopped at the interactive boundary.

Rename the conversation

Cmd-K → Rename Session → Save. Expected: the pane title and stored Session name change. Observed: both became Direct write verified.

Save a file

Open the changed .gitignore in Files, choose Edit, add a marker and Save. Expected: the change persists with recovery available. Observed: Desktop reported Saved. Previous file retained in recovery; the file on disk contains the marker.

Continue chatting

Focus the terminal and send a bounded prompt. Expected: the configured provider answers. Observed: DIRECT-WRITE-OK arrived in the same conversation.

Edit the Task description

On an unstarted Task, choose Edit description, change the text and Save; leave and return. Expected: the description persists. Observed: DESKTOP-NOTES-593 remained visible and was verified in SQLite. This second unstarted Task was prepared through CLI; the first Task above was created entirely in the app.

Telemetry follows the request

Rename, file save and description save all appear in the ordinary logs/lf.log, with distinct trace IDs and real server PID 31997. The shared CLI/server mutation path records outcome, diagnostics and duration without inventing an OS Process per request. Admitted writes finish even if the viewer disconnects; the client does not replay them.

Observed single server durations were 18 ms, 198 ms and 1795 ms respectively. These individual operations are not substitutes for the benchmark distribution.

Failures and limits stay visible

The private Machine could chat through the configured native provider but lacked a managed Codex account for autonomous research. Attempts to launch that Graph were refused; the fixture conversation was then told not to launch more. A completed research run is not proved.

The earlier server-cutover fixture failed when Desktop and the manually started server used different helper hashes. Matching the signed helper repaired that setup. Its failure screenshot is retained below.

The earlier full Desktop suite exposed fixture initialization and blocking-process waits; focused repairs passed. Final full-suite and Xcode checks remain owned by the running Task Graph. The native bundle predates later error formatting, stop attribution and provider-admission cwd refinements. Their automated checks are separate from these screenshots.

Source-built Swift and the comprehensive CLI/server parity suite passed, including concurrent requests, default telemetry, large saves and completion after disconnect. Remote routing also passed its no-local-fallback check. Publication and merge are separate; this page claims neither.

Latest follow-on validation: the expanded provider-cwd parity case failed on macOS /private/var/… versus /var/… path spelling. The live Graph owns the repair and rerun. Final validation and publication remain unfinished.
